title: Timeless engineering constraints
purpose: Constrain source changes and review toward low future change cost, local reasoning, single authority, explicit boundaries, and invariant-driven correctness without turning design judgment into a mechanical checklist.

constraint_semantics.conflict_rule: When principles collide, prefer the choice that reduces future change cost and reduces the number of things a maintainer must understand simultaneously in THIS codebase.
constraint_semantics.hard_rule: Expose the correct boundary with the minimum behavior-preserving refactor first; prove existing behavior still holds; then change behavior.
constraint_semantics.judgment_rule: Treat these as design constraints, not slogans. If literal application of a principle would increase future cost in this codebase, choose the lower-cost design and make the exception and evidence explicit in the durable review record.

principles.name: Separation of Concerns
principles.constraint: One kind of work per part: UI, domain, persistence, and infrastructure remain distinct unless a proven local simplification reduces future change cost.

principles.name: Encapsulation / Information Hiding
principles.constraint: Expose small stable contracts and hide implementation details behind them.

principles.name: High Cohesion + Loose Coupling
principles.constraint: Things that change together live together; independent parts communicate through narrow contracts.

principles.name: DRY
principles.constraint: Maintain one authoritative representation of each piece of knowledge. Similar-looking code may remain separate when it does not encode the same knowledge; avoid over-DRY.

principles.name: KISS
principles.constraint: Prefer the simplest design that satisfies current requirements; complexity is a long-term tax.

principles.name: Single Responsibility
principles.constraint: A unit should have one coherent reason to change.

principles.name: Depend on Abstractions
principles.constraint: Policy does not depend on implementation details; policy and details depend on explicit contracts.

principles.name: YAGNI
principles.constraint: Do not add speculative features, frameworks, extension hooks, or indirection for hypothetical future use.

principles.name: Composition over Inheritance
principles.constraint: Assemble behavior from focused pieces rather than growing fragile inheritance hierarchies.

principles.name: Open/Closed with discipline
principles.constraint: Extend at stable boundaries only after the same axis of change has appeared at least twice; do not pre-build extension systems.

principles.name: One Authority per Fact
principles.constraint: Every durable fact has exactly one authoritative owner and representation. Everything else derives, references, or explicitly caches it; never synchronize competing truths.

principles.name: Enforce Invariants at Boundaries
principles.constraint: Put correctness in schemas, state transitions, constraints, contracts, and acceptance gates rather than worker memory or procedural instructions; invalid transitions must be impossible or rejected immediately.

supporting_constraints: Law of Demeter: prefer local knowledge and narrow collaborator surfaces.
Fail fast and make illegal states unrepresentable where practical.
Optimize for deletion: make obsolete behavior easy to remove cleanly.
Unix discipline: do one thing well and compose through explicit contracts.
source_mutation_rules: Do not add a second path around an existing abstraction merely to make a task pass. If the abstraction is wrong, repair the abstraction first.
If two implementations encode the same domain knowledge, consolidate the authority before adding new behavior.
Use an existing stable extension boundary when one already fits; do not create a parallel framework.
A behavior-changing patch must preserve or improve local reasoning: the change should not require understanding unrelated layers to modify one concern.
When a behavior change requires a boundary repair, the behavior-preserving refactor must be independently reviewable and proven before the behavior change.

blocking_conditions: A new implementation path bypasses an existing appropriate abstraction instead of repairing it.
A durable fact gains a second competing authority without explicit replicated/read-model semantics.
A behavior-changing patch that requires a boundary repair combines the structural repair and behavioral change without independently proving preserved behavior.
Correctness depends only on worker instructions or call ordering when the invariant can be enforced at a schema, transition, contract, or acceptance boundary.
Speculative abstractions or extension points are introduced without demonstrated current need.
review_enforcement.evidence_rule: Review findings cite the concrete boundary, authority, invariant, or future-change-cost consequence. Principle names alone are not sufficient evidence.

invariants: These constraints are authoritative engineering knowledge for ClawKraft source mutation and review; other Programs reference this template instead of copying its full rule set.
The constraints do not create a second scheduler, task graph, acceptance authority, merge authority, or deployment authority.
Architecture judgment remains codebase-specific and evidence-backed; the constraint set is not a mechanical checklist.
